doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Backing into film scoring
summary: Mandel says Jack Lewis got him the job, that he did not push for film work, and that doors only opened again in the early 1960s after B pictures.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So you said you were hired to do the score because of Jack Lewis.
So at that time I gather that you weren't really consciously pushing for a film writing career.

I wasn't, I wasn’t, I did everything else in this business first, before I did movies and I just kind of backed into them rather than was out there rushing for them and I was, you know, I was happy doing what I was doing.
So how much did this advance your career as a film writer or your desire to do it or the doors opening for you to do more of it?

The doors didn't open again until the early 60s, you know 1963, ‘64, ‘65, then they opened wide but I had to wait five years. Then after that I did a couple of B pictures like, The 3rd Voice, I didn't enjoy them, I didn’t realize I'd started off with a great picture, great cast, great crew, wonderful producer who was Walter Wanger, and a marvelous director who was very kind, who was Robert Wise. And they encouraged me and I thought, wow, I like this, this is great and then I discovered it wasn’t like that out there, at all like that out there.
